entry: American stage actor and assassin of President [[Abraham Lincoln]]. A member of a prominent theatrical family from Maryland, Booth was a Confederate sympathizer who joined the Confederate Secret Service and opposed the recent abolition of slavery. He shot Lincoln at Ford's Theatre in [[Washington, D.C.]] on April 14, 1865, and Lincoln died the next morning. Booth was tracked down twelve days later in a barn in rural Virginia, where he was fatally shot. Of the eight conspirators convicted, four were hanged.

American composer and conductor known for orchestral film scores. Best known for his work with [[George Lucas]] and [[Steven Spielberg]], he composed the scores for *Star Wars*, *Jaws*, *E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial* and *Schindler's List*. He has received five Academy Awards, for the arrangement of *Fiddler on the Roof* (1971) and for *Jaws* (1975), *Star Wars* (1977), *E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial* (1982) and *Schindler's List* (1993). His 54 [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nominations make him the second-most-nominated person in the award's history, after [[Walt Disney]]. Williams was principal conductor of the Boston Pops from 1980 to 1993 and is its laureate conductor. He composed the theme music for the 1984 Summer Olympics and received a Kennedy Center Honor in 2004.

English Catholic priest, philosopher and reformer. A theology professor at the [[University of Oxford]], Wycliffe argued that the church should not own property and that clergy in mortal sin had no right to exercise authority. He opposed papal supremacy and clerical privilege. He is traditionally credited with a vernacular translation of the Bible into Middle English, although recent scholarship has questioned his role in it. His followers, later called Lollards, spread his ideas through preaching, and his writings were condemned as heretical at the Council of Constance (1415). His writings influenced the Czech reformer [[Jan Hus]], and his ideas are often considered a precursor of [[Protestantism]].

British novelist and former intelligence officer, the pen name of David John Moore Cornwell. He worked for [[MI5]] and [[MI6]] in the 1950s and 1960s. His third novel, *The Spy Who Came in from the Cold* (1963), became an international best-seller and allowed him to leave MI6 to write full time. Many of his espionage novels, including *Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy* (1974), have been adapted for film or television. In 2008 *The Times* named him one of the "50 greatest British writers since 1945." He became an Irish citizen near the end of his life.

Christian monk, priest, hymnographer and apologist, born in [[Damascus]]. A polymath, he wrote on law, theology, philosophy and music. He defended the veneration of [[Icon|icons]] against the iconoclastic policies of Emperors Leo III and Constantine V, and he distinguished honor from idolatry. He is one of the Fathers of the [[Eastern Orthodox Church]] and is regarded as a Doctor of the [[Catholic Church]], who is often called the Doctor of the Assumption for his writings on the Assumption of Mary. Hymns he composed are still used in Eastern Christian worship and in western Lutheranism at Easter. According to tradition, he ended his life at the monastery of Mar Saba near Jerusalem.

Spanish Carmelite friar, priest and mystic, a major figure of the [[Counter-Reformation]] in Spain. Influenced by [[Teresa of Ávila]], he helped found the Discalced Carmelites, who sought a return to the stricter observance of the original Carmelite rule. His poetry and his writings on the development of the soul are regarded as the summit of mystical Christian literature and among the greatest works of Spanish literature. He described the spiritual life as purgative, illuminative and unitive ways, separated by the "dark nights" of sense and soul. He was canonized in 1726 and declared a Doctor of the Church in 1926, earning the title "mystical doctor."

Apostle of [[Jesus]] and, by tradition, author of the *Gospel of John*. One of the Twelve Apostles in the New Testament, he was the son of Zebedee and the younger brother of James. Church Fathers identified him with John the Evangelist, John of Patmos and John the Elder, and claimed that he outlived the other apostles and was the only one to die of natural causes, although modern scholars are divided on these claims. Many Christian denominations believe he also wrote the three Johannine epistles and the *Book of Revelation*. Many modern scholars continue to affirm traditional authorship, while others propose alternatives such as John the Elder or a literary creation. Most scholars hold that the epistles and the *Book of Revelation* had different authors.

Itinerant Jewish preacher and prophet active near the [[Jordan River]] in the early 1st century AD. He preached a [[Baptism|baptism]] of repentance, and most biblical scholars agree that he baptized [[Jesus]]. The Gospels present him as the forerunner of Jesus, and he is revered as a prophet in [[Christianity]], [[Islam]], the Baháʼí Faith, the Druze faith and Mandaeism. According to the New Testament, Herod Antipas had him beheaded around AD 30 after John rebuked him for marrying Herodias, the wife of Herod's brother. The Roman historian [[Josephus]] states that he was executed at the fortress of Machaerus. Mandaeans, an ancient ethnoreligious group, regard him as their greatest and final prophet.

Hungarian and American mathematician, physicist, computer scientist and engineer. He contributed to the mathematical framework of [[Quantum mechanics|quantum physics]], to functional analysis and to [[Game theory|game theory]], and he introduced or codified concepts including cellular automata and the digital computer. His analysis of self-replication preceded the discovery of the structure of [[DNA]]. During World War II he worked on the [[Manhattan Project]], developing the mathematical models behind the explosive lenses used in an implosion-type [[Nuclear weapon|nuclear weapon]]. In the 1950s he chaired several Defense Department committees and played a key role in the design of the first [[Intercontinental ballistic missile|intercontinental ballistic missile]] programs in the United States. He received a Medal of Freedom, and a crater on the [[Moon]] is named for him.

Rock and roll song written and sung by [[Chuck Berry]] and released as a single in 1958. It peaked at number two on the Hot R&B Sides chart. The title hints at autobiographical elements, since Berry was born on Goode Avenue in [[St. Louis]]. Credited as "the first rock & roll hit about rock & roll stardom," the song has been covered by many artists, including Jimi Hendrix and the Sex Pistols. *Rolling Stone* ranked it 33rd on its 2021 list of 500 Greatest Songs of All Time and 7th on its 2004 list. It was one of the 27 songs on the *Voyager Golden Record*, and in 1999 it was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.

American comedian, writer and television host. He hosted *The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson* on [[NBC]] from 1962 to 1992, succeeding Jack Paar. His casual, conversational style and quick wit made him a cultural phenomenon. He won six Primetime Emmy Awards and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1992. He is widely regarded as the King of Late Night Television, and [[David Letterman]] is among those who have cited his influence.

American singer-songwriter whose music blended country, rockabilly, folk, blues and gospel. Known for his deep, bass-baritone voice and his all-black stage wardrobe, he was nicknamed "Man in Black." Born to poor cotton farmers in Arkansas, he grew up during the [[Great Depression]], and the hardship of that period shaped many of his songs. He rose to fame in the mid-1950s in the rockabilly scene of [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]], with signature songs including "Folsom Prison Blues," "I Walk the Line" and "Ring of Fire." He was known for free concerts in prisons and for later cover versions, including "Hurt" by [[Nine Inch Nails]]. Cash is among the best-selling music artists of all time, with more than 90 million records sold worldwide. He was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]], as well as the Country Music and Gospel Music halls of fame.

American actor, musician and filmmaker known for eccentric characters and his films with director [[Tim Burton]], beginning with *Edward Scissorhands* (1990). He gained worldwide fame as Jack Sparrow in the *Pirates of the Caribbean* series (2003–2017), and he received three Academy Award nominations for Best Actor. He was married to the actress Amber Heard from 2015 to 2017. The two later accused each other of [[Domestic violence|domestic abuse]]. In separate defamation cases, an English court ruled in 2020 that Depp had engaged in domestic abuse, and a Virginia court ruled in 2022 that Heard had defamed him.

American stunt performer, actor and producer, born Philip John Clapp in [[Knoxville, Tennessee|Knoxville]]. He co-created and starred in the [[MTV]] stunt series *Jackass* (2000–2001) and its film franchise, whose final installment, *Jackass: Best and Last*, was released in 2026. His film roles include *Men in Black II* (2002) and *The Dukes of Hazzard* (2005), and he voiced Leonardo in *Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles* (2014). Before his breakthrough he worked as a stand-in for [[Keanu Reeves]] on *Bram Stoker's Dracula* (1992).

American adult film performer, director and YouTuber, born Steven Wolfe in [[Pittsburgh]]. He moved to [[Los Angeles]] in 2006 to work full time in the adult film industry. As of April 2019 he had performed in more than 1,000 scenes for the studio Brazzers. He is known for his shaved head and muscular physique, and he has been the subject of [[Internet meme|internet memes]] about the variety of occupations his characters hold. He co-launched the [[YouTube]] channel SinsTV in 2017, which had more than 2.1 million subscribers as of January 2024. He has received multiple AVN Awards nominations and wins.

American Olympic swimmer, water polo player and actor. He won five Olympic gold medals, in the 100-meter freestyle, 400-meter freestyle and 4 × 200-meter relay at the 1924 Summer Olympics and in the 100-meter freestyle and relay in 1928. He also won a bronze medal in water polo in 1924. On July 9, 1922, he broke Duke Kahanamoku's world record in the 100-meter freestyle, swimming it in 58.6 seconds. After retiring from competition, he played Edgar Rice Burroughs's Tarzan in twelve feature films from 1932 to 1948, six for [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]] and six for RKO. He then starred in sixteen *Jungle Jim* films and filmed 26 half-hour episodes of a television series of the same name.

Private research university in [[Baltimore]], Maryland, named for the Quaker philanthropist Johns Hopkins. His bequest of $7 million, the largest philanthropic gift in U.S. history up to that time, established the university and the affiliated Johns Hopkins Hospital. Opened in 1876 under its first president, Daniel Coit Gilman, the university is considered the first research university in the United States, integrating teaching and research. It became a founding member of the Association of American Universities in 1900. Its School of Medicine, established in 1893, is internationally recognized for biomedical research. The men's [[Lacrosse|lacrosse]] team has won 44 national titles.

City (pop., 2020: 858,118), capital of the Malaysian state of Johor, at the southern tip of the [[Malay Peninsula]], bordering [[Singapore]]. The name Johor Bahru means "New Johor." Under Sultan Abu Bakar, who reigned from 1886 to 1895, the former fishing village was modernized with administrative centers, schools and a railway to Woodlands, Singapore. Japanese forces occupied the city during the [[Pacific War]]. In 1946 the political party UMNO was formed at the Istana Besar, and the city became a center of postwar Malay nationalism. Granted city status in 1994, it is part of Iskandar Malaysia, the nation's largest special economic zone by investment value. The Johor-Singapore Causeway gives it the busiest land border crossing in the world.

Connection between bones, ossicles or other hard structures of the [[Skeleton|skeletal system]] that permits movement. Joints are classified structurally, by the binding tissue that connects the bones, and functionally, by the degree of movement they allow. Joints such as the knee, elbow and shoulder are self-lubricating and can withstand compression and heavy loads. Sutures between the bones of the [[Skull]] permit very little movement, which protects the brain and sense organs. [[Osteoarthritis]] involves the breakdown of [[Cartilage]], causing pain and reduced mobility. Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disorder that causes chronic inflammation in the joints, and [[Gout]] arises from the accumulation of uric acid crystals in them.

Short humorous story, usually with dialogue, that ends in a punch line. The linguist Robert Hetzron defined a joke as a short humorous piece of oral literature in which the funniness culminates in the final sentence. Jokes benefit from brevity, and the shaggy dog story is an anti-joke that deliberately withholds a punch line. Jokes are passed along anonymously, in private conversation, in scripted entertainment and, more recently, online. The oldest identified joke is a [[Sumer|Sumerian]] proverb from about 1900 BC with toilet humor. The second oldest, from [[Ancient Egypt]] c. 1600 BC, was discovered on the Westcar Papyrus.

Fictional supervillain in comic books published by [[DC Comics]] and the archenemy of [[Batman]]. Created by Bill Finger, Bob Kane and Jerry Robinson, the character first appeared in the debut issue of *Batman* on April 25, 1940. Unlike most comic book characters, the Joker has no definitive origin story; the most common version involves a fall into a tank of chemical waste. He has no superhuman abilities and relies on chemical expertise to create poisons and weapons. In *The Killing Joke* (1988) he paralyzed Barbara Gordon. Heath Ledger played the character in *The Dark Knight* (2008).

Kenyan anti-colonial activist and politician, prime minister (1963–1964) and first president of Kenya (1964–1978). He led the Kenya African National Union (KANU) and oversaw Kenya's transition from a colony of the [[British Empire]] into an independent republic. In 1952 he was convicted of masterminding the Mau Mau uprising, a charge he denied, and he was held in detention until 1961. As president he moved toward a one-party state, suppressed political dissent and promoted reconciliation between indigenous groups and the European minority. Kenya joined the [[Commonwealth of Nations|Commonwealth]] under him, and his government pursued a pro-Western, anti-communist foreign policy during the [[Cold War]]. Supporters honored him as the Father of the Nation, while critics called his rule dictatorial and cited widespread corruption.

American former mixed martial artist who competed from 2008 to 2025 and held championships in the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]]. He was a two-time light heavyweight champion and held the heavyweight title from 2023 to 2025. He became the youngest champion in UFC history at age 23, defeating Maurício Rua. His only professional loss was a disqualification against Matt Hamill, a result disputed by Hamill and UFC president Dana White. Between 2015 and 2017 he lost the light heavyweight title three times through disciplinary action. Jones retired in 2025.

American comedian, writer and television host, best known as host of *The Daily Show* on Comedy Central from 1999 to 2015. The program gained critical acclaim under him for satirical commentary on news and politics. Earlier he hosted *The Jon Stewart Show* on [[MTV]] (1993–1995). In 2010 he and [[Stephen Colbert]] headlined the Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear. After leaving *The Daily Show* he advocated for 9/11 first responders and veterans exposed to toxic burn pits, and he helped pass the PACT Act of 2022. He hosted the 78th and 80th Academy Awards.

American actor known for intense character roles. He won the Academy Award for Best Actor for playing a paraplegic Vietnam veteran in *Coming Home* (1978) and was nominated for *Midnight Cowboy* (1969), *Runaway Train* (1985) and *Ali* (2001). His other films include *Deliverance* (1972), *Heat* (1995), *Mission: Impossible* (1996) and *National Treasure* (2004). He won his fourth Golden Globe Award in 2014 for playing Mickey Donovan in the Showtime series *Ray Donovan*. In 2019 he received the National Medal of Arts. He is the father of actress [[Angelina Jolie]].
